title: CoreDNS Conntrack Table Saturation causing Intermittent Resolution Failures

impact.user_impact_summary: Order confirmation emails and push notifications were delayed up to 25 minutes.

five_whys.question: Why were emails delayed?
five_whys.answer: The notification-gateway could not resolve the SMTP relay DNS hostname.

five_whys.question: Why did DNS lookups time out?
five_whys.answer: Linux kernel conntrack tables on the worker nodes reached 100% capacity and began dropping UDP packets.

five_whys.question: Why were conntrack tables saturated with UDP connections?
five_whys.answer: NodeLocal DNSCache was not deployed on the cluster, causing all pods to query upstream CoreDNS over UDP.

five_whys.question: Why did notification-gateway generate excessive DNS queries?
five_whys.answer: An updated client library disabled connection pooling and reopened TCP connections on every email dispatch.

five_whys.question: Why was NodeLocal DNSCache not enabled by default?
five_whys.answer: Cluster provisioning templates for eu-central-1 were running on an older Terraform module version.

what_went_well: Circuit breaker in email-worker queued failed deliveries for retry without dropping data.
what_went_poorly: Missing alert on node conntrack utilization allowed issue to manifest as DNS timeouts first.
where_we_got_lucky: No transactional checkout endpoints were directly blocked by the notification queue.

action_items.description: Deploy NodeLocal DNSCache DaemonSet across all Kubernetes clusters.
